hold_text: Tier-2 by two independent routes: it changes a LIVE API's auth behaviour, and on this repo MERGING IS THE DEPLOY (ict-git-sync pulls every ~5 min; there is no separate install step). The operator approved DOING this work on 2026-09-09 — put as a four-option decision (gate /api/bot/db/* now · full Phase H · accept and record · measure the blast radius first), and they chose 'gate now'. That approves the work, NOT the deploy, and the deploy is what needs the second OK. ⚠️ DO NOT MERGE THIS ON A GREEN CI. Two preconditions are MEASURED-FALSE right now and merging before they are fixed takes the SPA's Data Explorer tab from working to permanently 401 with no way in. (1) THE SPA CANNOT SEND A BEARER: ict-trader-dashboard has exactly one fetch call site (webapp/src/lib/api.ts::get<T>) sending only Accept: application/json, and a search across all 40 .ts/.svelte/.js files under webapp/src/ for Authorization|Bearer|api/auth/login|jwt returns ZERO matches — there is no login screen and no token store. (2) THE HOST CANNOT MINT A BEARER: POST /api/auth/login against ict-bot.duckdns.org returns 500 auth_unavailable, i.e. ALLOWED_EMAIL / WEBAPP_PASSWORD_SHA256 are unset on the live VM. Fixing (2) is a Tier-2 set-env on the VM; fixing (1) is a change in the OTHER repo, which this session has read-only access to. Neither is in this diff and neither was widened into it. ⚠️ The dispatch brief for this work asserted the SPA 'already holds a session for other gated routes'. That premise is FALSE and was checked rather than inherited: docs/api-tier-policy.md § 2a said in terms 'No consumer has ever called these', and the SPA source confirms it. This is exactly the 'gating breaks a consumer path nobody enumerated' case the brief said to REPORT BEFORE SHIPPING rather than widen or abandon — so the gate is built, validated and held. The recommended order is: set the VM auth envs → ship SPA login → merge this. ⚠️ NOT the diag-token question. /api/diag/* is bearer-gated and its exposure is a DECIDED, accepted risk that CLAUDE.md forbids reopening. This is a DIFFERENT surface that carries no credential of any kind, and the two must not be collapsed.
why: Attaches Depends(require_session) to the two /api/bot/db/* routes (db_tables, db_table) under BL-20260901-DB-EXPLORER-SERVES-21-MORE-TABLES-UNAUTHENTICATED-INCLUDING-2-3M-SIGNAL-ROWS. POPULATION STATED: exactly 2 routes exist under /api/bot/db/*, enumerated by AST over src/web/api/routers/ joining each @router.<verb> to its APIRouter(prefix=...) — both were ungated, both are now gated, none left behind, and a test asserts that count so a third route added later without a gate fails in CI rather than on a public host. MEASURED UNAUTHENTICATED AGAINST THE LIVE HOST 2026-09-09, no bearer: GET /api/bot/db/tables → 200, 10,494 bytes, 21 tables with full column schemas; GET /api/bot/db/table/trades → 200 with REAL ROWS, total 5589 over 41 columns including account_id, broker_order_id, entry_price and exit_price; signals total 2,639,949; order_packages 4,500. The row-serving half was previously reported but UNVERIFIED — it is now established first-hand. The 2026-09-01 _TABLE_ALLOWLIST is the AUTHORIZATION layer and never closed this (verified working: device_tokens 404s); WO-20260901-PHASE-H states the distinction directly. NO ROUTE BEHAVIOUR OTHER THAN AUTH CHANGES: no query, projection, allowlist, redaction, pagination or filter_state semantics touched. src/runtime/ order paths, config/ and deploy/ are untouched. TESTS: 26 existing tests kept and now run authenticated — none weakened — plus 8 new gate tests; 34 pass. NEGATIVE CONTROL RUN: with the gate stripped, exactly the 8 new tests fail and all 26 originals still pass, so the new tests genuinely detect the gate's absence and the originals are unaffected in either direction. The gate is proven to fail CLOSED when auth is unconfigured (401 before any env read), which is the polarity that matters given the live host's envs are unset. Docs: the two rows MOVE from Tier 1 to Tier 2a in docs/api-tier-policy.md (a row there is CI-required and a row in the API reference is not a substitute), the reference rows are corrected, and Tier 1's stale hand-count is fixed — it read '70 of the 96 routes' where a mechanical count gives 76 of 105.
